Procedural reasoning

PLANNER makes reasoning procedures programmable

A problem-solving language connected assertions and goals with procedures that controlled inference.

Carl Hewitt

AI topics

Explore related entries. Larger tags appear on more entries.

ReasoningPlanningSymbolic AITools & frameworksKnowledge representation

The contribution

PLANNER organized reasoning around patterns, goals, and procedures selected when relevant conditions were met. Its language supported adding or withdrawing assertions and breaking goals into subgoals. Hewitt made the control of deduction part of the programming language, linking knowledge representation with the procedures that use that knowledge.

What this does not establish

This paper presents a language and problem-solving approach. Its title is not evidence of a general-purpose autonomous robot; successful reasoning still depends on suitable knowledge and procedures.

Why this date?

1969 dates the original IJCAI paper. SHRDLU reference 27 cites it separately from a revised PLANNER memorandum in reference 28.

Cited by later work in the Atlas

  • SHRDLU grounds language in a small world (1971). Reference 27 cites the 1969 conference paper; the later memorandum is a separate reference. Check the reference list.
